newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-KNICKS' STARKS WINS SIXTH MAN AWARD.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-KNICKS' STARKS WINS SIXTH MAN AWARD.

text.p: New York Knicks guard John Starks, second on the team in steals and third in scoring and assists, was named the winner of the NBA's Sixth Man Award on Wednesday.
Starks received 84 out of a possible 115 votes from a panel of sports writers and broadcasters throughout the United States and Canada.

Chicago Bulls forward Toni Kukoc, the Sixth Man Award winner last year, finished second with seven votes. Forward Chris Gatling, traded from the Dallas Mavericks to the New Jersey Nets in February, was third with six votes.
Starks averaged 13.8 points, 2.8 assists, 2.7 rebounds and 1.17 steals while coming off the bench in 76 of the 77 games he played this season.
Starks became the second Knick player in three years to win the award. Forward Anthony Mason, traded by New York to Charlotte last July for forward Larry Johnson, won the honour in 1994-95.

Starks had several standout performances during the season. He had 31 points, five assists and two steals in a 110-107 overtime loss at Indiana on April 14 and made the game-winning three-point field goal in a 103-101 victory over the Chicago Bulls last Saturday.
The 115-member voting panel consisted of 28 national media members and three media members who cover the NBA regularly from each of the league's 29 cities.
